problem_type: Canvas drag end guard cancels a different pointer on the same stage
symptom: A pointercancel from another pointer or another stage can clear data-dragging before the active pointerup, causing an active canvas gesture to lose its lease.
direct_cause: The shared stage-level gesture end guard treated an untracked lease as a match for every pointer event, so a tracked pointer on one stage could schedule fallback cancellation on another stage.
class_root: The global fallback guard must correlate pointer events with tracked lease identities and must not manufacture a match for untracked leases on an unrelated stage.
affected_population: Canvas pointer and resize gesture cleanup in reduced or headless window hosts
Vitest and future non-browser consumers of the shared drag lease
internal_only_reason: The scheduler fallback is an application-owned host boundary; browser requestAnimationFrame semantics are used when available and the deferred timer is only a compatibility path for reduced hosts.

invariant_owner_layer.why: The canvasDraggingFlag module owns the lease lifecycle and is the only place that schedules the deferred end guard; its focused test covers the lease ordering and cancellation contract.

invariants: A stage-level pointer end event only arms fallback cleanup when a lease on that stage has the same tracked pointer identity.
A different pointer cancellation leaves every unrelated stage and untracked lease intact until its own targeted interruption or release.

door_reduction.why_not: The lease lifecycle has six write callers and fifteen read callers by design; this fix changes only the shared deferred scheduling boundary and does not merge independent gesture owners or host consumers.

generality_proof: All canvas gesture owners converge on beginCanvasDragging and the stage guard; pointer identity is checked once at that shared boundary.

shared_boundaries.responsibility: Register pointer identity with the shared lease and filter stage-level gesture end events before fallback cleanup.

same_class_entry_points.evidence: Uses beginCanvasDragging and receives the shared pointer filter.

recurrence.reason: Any multi-pointer stage can deliver an unrelated pointercancel while the shared fallback guard is armed.
same_class_scan: Checked all listed drag lease readers and writers.

prevention.invariant: The shared stage fallback filters pointer end events against the live lease pointer identity before disarming or cancelling.
prevention.failure_mode: Unrelated pointer events are ignored; the active gesture remains visible and is cleaned up by its matching end event.
prevention.strategy: Keep host capability detection in the shared lease module so gesture callers do not grow per-host fallbacks.

legacy_paths.rationale: The shared CanvasDragLease remains the only drag lifecycle path; only its scheduler capability branch was hardened.

dependency_lifecycle.rationale: No dependency is added or upgraded; the fallback uses the host timer already available to the runtime.

migration: No persisted data or public caller contract changes.
residual_risks: Callers that omit pointerId rely on their own targeted interruption listeners; a global pointer event cannot prove their identity and therefore does not arm another stage's fallback.
